match.reason: No point in the bank covers the costs and benefits of inequality itself, since the costs of growth point only names inequality as one possible side effect of growth.

draft.title: Costs and benefits of inequality
card: Benefit
Some inequality can reward effort, skill and risk-taking. The chance of higher pay or profit can give people a reason to work hard, train and start businesses.
Cost
Large gaps can harm health, because lower-income households may struggle to afford good food, housing and medical care.
Cost
Large gaps can weaken social cohesion, which is the sense of trust and shared belonging in a community. They can also slow economic growth.
Cost
People left behind may not get the education or training they need. Their skills go unused, so the economy produces less than it could.
draft.remember: Some inequality can reward effort and risk, but large gaps can harm health, cohesion and growth.

a.q: Which is a possible benefit of some inequality?
opts: It can reward effort, skill and risk-taking
It can improve the health of low-income households
It can strengthen trust between all groups
It can make full use of everyone's skills
a.why: Higher pay or profit can give people a reason to work, train and take risks. The other options are harms that the card links to large gaps, not benefits.
a.clue: Think about what the chance of higher pay gives people.

b.q: Jaya, a talented student in a low-income suburb, cannot afford training and takes unskilled work. How does this show a cost of inequality?
opts: Her skills are wasted, so output is lower than it could be
Her low pay rewards her for taking a risk
Her suburb gains from stronger social cohesion
Her training costs lift economic growth
b.why: When people left behind cannot develop their skills, the economy loses what they could have produced. Low pay here does not reward effort or risk, so the reward option is wrong.
b.clue: Ask what the economy loses when skills go unused.

a.best: It can reward effort, skill and risk-taking

b.best: Her skills are wasted, so output is lower than it could be

problems.detail: Why (a) says the other options 'are harms that the card links to large gaps'. They are not harms. They are good outcomes (trust, health, full use of skills) that large gaps can damage, so the explanation could confuse students.

It can improve the health of low-income households
It can strengthen trust between all groups
It can make full use of everyone's skills
a.why: Higher pay or profit can give people a reason to work, train and take risks. The other options describe good outcomes, such as health, trust and full use of skills, that large gaps can damage. They are not things inequality brings.
a.clue: Think about what the chance of higher pay gives people.

b.q: Jaya, a talented student in a low-income suburb, cannot afford training and takes unskilled work. How does this show a cost of inequality?
opts: Her ability goes unused, so the economy produces less
Her low pay rewards risk, so she has a reason to train
Her suburb grows closer, so social cohesion is stronger
Her lower wage costs less, so economic growth speeds up
b.why: Jaya is left behind without training, so her ability is never used and the economy produces less than it could. The risk option is wrong: her low pay comes from lacking money for training, not from a risk she chose to take.
b.clue: Think about what Jaya could have produced with training.
